producer_checks.information_cutoff: After 13 Nov 2026 completed US and Brazilian sessions, 14 Nov Saturday BRT; no Saturday session claimed.
producer_checks.novelty: 13 Nov published IEA oil balance and BLS October PPI measured after previous report cutoff, together with 13 Nov completed Treasury/stock closes, Eurostat Q3 GDP and IBGE September retail.
producer_checks.bilingual_parity: Ten aligned analytical sections and sources; two charts with identical numeric sequences, matching time vintage, table/flow/map semantic parity.
producer_checks.visual_evidence: Two audited charts: US PPI October monthly subindices and official Treasury 10-year observations dated 10/12/13 November; dated evidence table, conditional flow, regional map, scenario matrix.
producer_checks.source_check: BLS, Treasury, IEA, Eurostat, ONS, China NBS, BCB; Reuters, AP, Estadão and Agencia Brasil. Oil annual projections are not subtracted from October observed supply.
producer_checks.editorial_status: Producer staged only; independent SHA-bound QA approval required prior to public bundle creation.

limitations: No independent high-frequency survey of global corporate credit spreads or exact portfolio fund flows.
IEA forecast supply surplus is prospective; Gulf shipping risk and diesel/product availability remain uncertain.
British and euro-area Q3 GDP estimates are preliminary.
Brazilian fiscal package still faces additional legislative steps.
contrary_evidence: Higher observed crude supply does not establish cheaper delivered diesel, but it reduces crude scarcity pressures.
Lower US monthly PPI does not imply lower annual inflation, and the next Fed decision is not predetermined.
Higher Treasury yields do not demonstrate cancelled AI investment or uniformly higher private loan rates.
Brazilian monthly retail increase does not reverse weak quarterly comparison.

en.title: Global Macro — Oil supply recovers, but diesel scarcity and US inflation keep the cost of capital elevated
en.deck: IEA signals a prospective crude surplus while refined fuels remain strained; US PPI and Treasury yields prolong financing pressure.
en.regime: Crude supply rebalances while refined-product bottlenecks and high dollar funding costs persist.
en.key_risk: A forecast oil surplus is mistaken for delivered fuel disinflation; loan credit-spread effects remain unverified.
